page: Amazon Web Services r5.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier. However, multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks reach average levels within the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests, including uncached read and write operations at 79.24 GB/sec and 48.62 GB/sec respectively, also align with average performance tiers. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average speeds, processing 13.23 million operations per second.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, the r5.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-core compute speeds or local NVMe storage. The lack of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as database operations, caching layers, web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
